strengths: Extensive and rigorous empirical evaluation across many datasets (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10/100), tasks (supervised classification, unsupervised representation learning, combined supervised/unsupervised, multimodal learning, occlusion robustness), and baselines (discPC, genPC, hybridPC, and their BP counterparts), with multiple seeds and reported error bars.

The proposed bPC model addresses a genuine limitation of prior PC models (discPC's inability to generate coherently, genPC/hybridPC's poor classification), and the empirical results convincingly show it matches or exceeds unidirectional/hybrid models in their specialized domains simultaneously.

The energy-landscape analysis (Section 4.4, XOR toy example and MNIster sampling experiment with Inception/FID scores) provides a compelling and interpretable mechanistic explanation for why bidirectional coupling helps avoid overconfident or biased minima, going beyond simple benchmark numbers.

Strong supplementary material with detailed hyperparameter search protocols, additional baseline models (arbitrary-graph PC, shared-weight bPC, decay discPC), ablations on the αgen/αdisc ratio, and analysis of architectural choices (max-pooling artefacts), which supports reproducibility and thoroughness.

The biologically relevant experiments (multimodal association learning and inference under occlusion) are well-motivated and provide additional evidence of the practical/biological value of bidirectional processing beyond standard ML benchmarks.
weaknesses: The core technical contribution is relatively incremental: bPC is essentially the sum of the previously proposed genPC and discPC energy functions without a stop-gradient, which is a fairly natural combination once the ingredients are known; the novelty lies mostly in this being tested and shown to be non-trivial rather than a fundamentally new mechanism.

bPC always uses twice the neurons/parameters compared to standalone discPC or genPC (matching hybridPC), which somewhat clouds efficiency claims (e.g., 'half the neurons' framing in 4.1 is only relative to running two separate unidirectional networks, not an absolute efficiency gain over hybridPC).

Performance still noticeably lags behind BP-based models in more complex settings (e.g., CIFAR-10 classification in the combined task without max-pooling drops ~25%, and CIFAR reconstruction RMSE remains higher than AE/hybridBP), somewhat undercutting the claim that bPC closes the gap with BP-based methods in harder tasks.

The precision/weighting parameters (αgen, αdisc) are manually tuned rather than learned, which is acknowledged as a simplification but weakens the biological plausibility narrative, since the brain would presumably need some mechanism to set/adapt these online.

Biological plausibility claims remain largely conceptual; there is no direct comparison to neural or behavioral data (e.g., no fits to physiological recordings), so the paper's biological relevance rests on architectural analogy rather than empirical validation against brain data.

The comparison to Qiu et al.'s bidirectional PC model (which reportedly performs well on both tasks) is dismissed primarily on plausibility grounds without empirical benchmarking, leaving open whether bPC's performance advantage over ALL bidirectional alternatives is as strong as claimed.

Some artefact issues (grid-like artefacts from max-pooling in generative reconstructions) are only partially resolved, and the fix reduces classification accuracy, indicating that architectural integration of bidirectional pathways still requires ad hoc trade-offs rather than a fully principled solution.

strengths: Addresses a well-motivated gap: unifying generative and discriminative predictive coding into a single biologically plausible energy function, whereas prior unidirectional or hybrid PC models sacrifice performance in one domain.

Very extensive empirical validation across many settings: supervised classification, unsupervised representation/distribution learning, joint supervised+unsupervised learning, multimodal/bimodal learning, robustness to missing/occluded inputs, and scaling to deep VGG architectures on CIFAR-10/100 and Tiny-ImageNet.

Strong set of baselines and ablations, including discPC, genPC, hybridPC, their backprop counterparts, an autoencoder, a VAE, arbitrary-graph PC, weight-shared bPC, and parameter-count-matched controls, which substantially strengthens the empirical claims.

Provides an interpretable mechanistic explanation (via energy landscape visualization on XOR and MNIST) for why bidirectional prediction yields sharper, better-calibrated minima than unidirectional models, connecting empirical results to a conceptual account.
Neural/circuit implementation is described with local, Hebbian-compatible computations, maintaining biological plausibility claims and linking to dendritic error-computation literature.
Thorough and transparent supplementary material with detailed architectures, hyperparameter search spaces, training procedures, and compute reporting, aiding reproducibility.
weaknesses: The core technical contribution (linearly combining Egen and Edisc into one energy with two scalar weights) is conceptually a fairly direct combination of two existing PC formulations rather than a fundamentally new mechanism; novelty is somewhat incremental relative to hybridPC.

Performance is sensitive to the discriminative/generative weighting (αdisc/αgen), which must be hand-tuned per task (shown in SM D) and even differs between the free/fixed neuron subsets in the combined task (Section 4.3/SM A.5) — this undercuts the claim of a single flexible energy function and raises biological-plausibility concerns about how such precision-like parameters would be learned in vivo (the paper acknowledges this as future work only).

The efficiency argument (bPC uses half the value neurons of separate genPC+discPC pipelines) is a somewhat selective comparison, since bPC still requires twice the error neurons and separate weight matrices, and the paper does not quantify total computational/energetic cost fairly against alternatives.

Generative quality in deeper convolutional architectures suffers from grid-like artifacts due to max-pooling, and removing max-pooling to fix this substantially reduces classification accuracy (~25 point drop on CIFAR-10 in SM E), indicating the architecture does not yet cleanly reconcile both objectives at scale.

Comparisons to other biologically-plausible bidirectional models mentioned in related work (e.g., correlative information maximization, Symmetric Predictive Estimator) are discussed but not empirically benchmarked, leaving open how bPC compares to these alternatives beyond PC-specific baselines.

Hyperparameter tuning cost is very large (hundreds of GPU-hours per dataset), and some architecture-specific engineering choices (e.g., separate scaling for free vs. fixed neurons in xL) suggest a degree of task-specific tuning that may limit generality of the claimed "single energy function" solution.

strengths: The paper is extremely thorough empirically: it compares bPC against discPC, genPC, hybridPC, several backpropagation-matched baselines, an autoencoder, a VAE, arbitrary-graph PC, shared-weight bPC, and decay-based discPC, across MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10/100, and Tiny-ImageNet.

The supplementary material is unusually detailed and reproducible, with full architecture tables, hyperparameter search spaces, training algorithms, and compute budgets reported, which is a genuine strength for reproducibility.

The parameter-count-matched control experiments (SM G) and the XOR energy-landscape visualization (Section 4.4) provide a reasonable mechanistic explanation for why unidirectional PC models fail at the complementary task, adding some interpretive value beyond pure benchmarking.

Demonstrating that the approach scales to deeper VGG architectures on CIFAR-100/Tiny-ImageNet (Section 4.6) and still shows benefits under occlusion is a non-trivial scaling result that many biologically-plausible-learning papers fail to provide.
The biologically relevant occlusion and bimodal-learning experiments are a nice applied contribution beyond pure benchmark matching.
weaknesses: The core technical contribution is a fairly straightforward additive combination of two already-published energy functions (Eq. 1 and Eq. 2 summed with two extra scalar weights), which is conceptually incremental relative to genPC/discPC and to prior bidirectional models (Xu et al. 2017; Bozkurt et al. 2023; Qiu et al. 2023) that the paper itself cites as precedent; the differentiation from these mainly rests on implementation details (separate weights, no shared parameters) rather than a fundamentally new mechanism.

bPC roughly doubles the number of value/weight parameters relative to a single unidirectional model (two full sets of top-down and bottom-up weights), and while SM G attempts a parameter-matched comparison, the main figures in Sections 4.1-4.3 largely compare bPC (2x parameters) against single-pathway baselines, which somewhat overstates the apparent advantage in several plots.

The method depends on hand-tuned scalar precision weights (alpha_gen, alpha_disc) that must be carefully balanced per task (shown to be quite sensitive in SM D, with training instability when badly set); the paper acknowledges this as future work rather than resolving it, which undercuts the claim of a unified, principled energy function.

Several claimed 'wins' are modest or task-dependent: bPC sometimes underperforms discPC/BP on pure classification (Table 10, Fig. 3B) and genPC/hybridPC on pure generation RMSE by small margins, and the generative advantage over discPC is somewhat unsurprising given discPC was never designed for generation.

The biological plausibility claims are somewhat overstated: the model requires two independent sets of synaptic weights per connection (bottom-up and top-down) without weight symmetry, plus separate error populations for each direction, which is a substantially larger and more specific circuit assumption than is empirically justified by cited neuroscience evidence.

Evaluation relies on relatively small models/datasets (MLP with 256 hidden units, small CNN/VGG variants) with only 5 seeds; several key comparisons (Section 4.6) show large accuracy differences between very similar models trained with the same hyperparameters copied from discPC without additional tuning for bPC, raising questions about whether baselines were optimally tuned in the deep-model experiments.

The paper does not compare to non-PC biologically-plausible bidirectional learning approaches (e.g., target propagation variants, contrastive Hebbian learning) that also blend feedforward/feedback signals, limiting the positioning of the contribution within the broader biologically-plausible learning literature.
